subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- November 03, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - November 03, 2026

Dear AcreetionOS community,

As we continue to move forward with our mission to provide a user-friendly and privacy-focused Linux distribution, we want to take a moment to highlight some recent developments and updates in the AcreetionOS ecosystem.

Firstly, we'd like to acknowledge the recent release of Tor Browser 16.0, which has been making waves in the security community. This new version offers improved performance and security features, and we're excited to see the impact it will have on our users' online experiences.

In other news, our team has been hard at work on various projects, including the experimental Wayland Edition of AcreetionOS. This new feature is still in its early stages, but we're excited to see where it will take us. We've also been working on updating our wallpaper carousel, which now features a sleek new design and a fresh set of images.

On the development front, we've seen some exciting commits from our team members. Cobra3282000 has been working on updating our immutable infrastructure, while Natalie has been busy with various tasks, including fixing issues in the AcreetionOS-Xlibre repository.

We'd also like to take a moment to highlight the importance of security in our community. Recently, the Google Threat Intelligence blog published an article about the XCPE botnet, which highlights the need for vigilance and awareness when it comes to online threats. We're committed to providing a secure and safe environment for our users, and we encourage everyone to stay informed and take steps to protect themselves online.

As we move forward, we're excited to see the impact that our community will have on the world of Linux and beyond. We're proud to be a part of this community, and we're grateful for the support and contributions that we've received so far.

In other news, we've been working on improving our documentation and resources for users. We've added new guides and tutorials to our wiki, and we're always looking for ways to make it easier for users to get started with AcreetionOS.

We'd like to take a moment to thank our community for their continued support and engagement. Your feedback and contributions are invaluable to us, and we're grateful for the opportunity to work with such a passionate and dedicated group of individuals.

As always, we're committed to providing a user-friendly and privacy-focused Linux distribution that meets the needs of our users. We're excited to see what the future holds, and we look forward to continuing to work together to make AcreetionOS the best it can be.

Thank you for being part of the AcreetionOS community, and we look forward to seeing what the future holds.

Best regards,
Natalie Cole-Clift Spiva and Darren Clift
